Sara (Support): FYI customer 'acme' opened a ticket — after we enabled OIDC + SCIM they see 403s when users try to open the project console. They report 'works for some users, but most get 403'.
Sara (Support): Customer provided a screenshot: console shows "403 Permission denied" with no helpful detail. Happening since ~9:12am UTC after the idp provisioning change.
Customer (acme-admin): Confirmed — some users were converted from AD group sync. After migrating to new IdP, they can't access project pages. We see 403 on /console/projects and also API calls return 403.
Jamie - Platform: Can you paste a repro curl and a user id that gets 403? Also which org id?
Customer (acme-admin): org=org_7382, user jane.doe@acme.com. Repro: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer ey..." https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/projects/org_7382/projects``` Response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"forbidden","reason":"insufficient_role"}
Alex M.: Thanks. Quick hypothesis: SCIM provisioning events may be delayed and role assignment hasn't landed even though account exists. Another possibility: inherited deny rule accidentally applied during group mapping.
Sara (Support): Customer says SCIM shows users as 'active' in their IdP. They also did a manual re-invite on one user and that fixed it.
Jamie - Platform: Can we check our provisioning events for org_7382? @IDP Bot, can you show last SCIM events for that org?
IDP Bot: SCIM events (org_7382): 2025-11-16T09:09:12Z -> provisioning:create: queued; 2025-11-16T09:11:05Z -> provisioning:apply: partial_success; 2025-11-16T09:18:23Z -> provisioning:complete
Niko (Security): partial_success is suspicious — may indicate roles mapping failed for group(s). If role binding fails for a group, members can end up without project-level roles and get 403s. Also check for any 'inherited_deny' flags on affected projects.
Alex M.: Reproduced locally by forcing a user with no project role: API returns 403 as customer saw. Example debug output from our auth check: ```AUTH CHECK: user=jane.doe@acme.com org=org_7382 project=proj_91 roles=[] inherited_deny=false -> result=403```
Alex M.: Then ran a simulated partial mapping where group -> role binding failed: ```AUTH CHECK: roles=[] inherited_deny=true -> result=403 (inherited deny)```
Jamie - Platform: Ok, two things to try for a quick mitigation for the customer: 1) Manually re-sync SCIM for the org, 2) Re-apply role bindings for affected projects (we can do via admin CLI).
Sara (Support): Customer asked for a step-by-step workaround they can run themselves.
Alex M.: Workaround commands (admin or support-run): ```# resync provisioning
redwoodctl scim resync --org org_7382
# reapply group mappings for project proj_91
redwoodctl roles apply --org org_7382 --project proj_91 --mapping-file mappings/acme-defaults.yaml
# temporary: grant the user a project-viewer role until mapping completes
redwoodctl users grant-role --org org_7382 --project proj_91 --user jane.doe@acme.com --role project.viewer
``` Use with care; that last command is a temporary bandaid.
Customer (acme-admin): Ran resync, still seeing 403 on ~5 users. Re-applying mappings helped for one project but not across all projects.
Niko (Security): If reapplying mapping is inconsistent, check for conflicting deny rules. Query example for internal debug (eng only): ```SELECT id, type, scope, source FROM role_policies WHERE org_id='org_7382' AND scope LIKE 'project:%' AND policy='deny';``` If you see an inherited deny on a parent org/project, that will block access even if role exists.
Jamie - Platform: I checked our policy store for org_7382: found one inherited deny created by an automated migration job (job_id=mig-2025-11-16-09). That explains why some users were blocked after partial mapping. We'll remove the deny after confirming safety. :thinking:
Alex M.: Quick safety check: policy removal will not escalate privileges beyond intended group mappings because mappings will be reapplied immediately. I will schedule the removal and then re-run SCIM apply.
IDP Bot: Admin action scheduled: remove-policy policy_id=pol_4492 for org_7382 by alex.m at 09:34:12Z.
Alex M.: Removed pol_4492 and re-ran mapping apply across projects. Observed SCIM events: 09:36:05Z -> apply:start, 09:37:40Z -> apply:success.
Customer (acme-admin): After the policy removal + reapply, affected users can access console pages again. Confirmed for 7 users. Thanks! :thumbsup:
Sara (Support): Closing loop — customer verified fix. Root cause: automated migration introduced an inherited deny policy while SCIM mapping was only partially applied; users ended up with no effective roles. Resolution path: remove unintended deny, run a full SCIM resync, ensure mapping completes.
Jamie - Platform: Follow-up action: add a guard to migration jobs to avoid creating denies unless mapping success confirmed. Filed as PLATFORM-1223.
Niko (Security): Also adding an audit alert to detect newly-created deny policies in orgs with recent provisioning activity.
Sara (Support): Marking resolved and adding notes to the support ticket. If customer sees recurrence after IdP changes we'll re-open.
Sara (Support): thread closed.
